issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for class Ride: the problem statement (UML) and the exercise instructions require Ride to have two attributes (name: String, abbreviation: char) and to provide a public constructor that takes all attributes in the order shown. The solution implementation of Ride provides only a single-parameter constructor Ride(String name) and sets abbreviation to a fixed default ('A'). At the same time, several subclasses in the solution (RollerCoaster, LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) call super(name, abbreviation) expecting a two-parameter Ride constructor. This contradicts the UML/instructions and creates a compile-time / design inconsistency and student confusion about the required Ride constructor and how to initialize abbreviation.
issues.suggested_fix: Make Ride's constructor match the UML and the exercise instructions: declare public Ride(String name, char abbreviation) and assign both attributes from parameters (do not hardcode a default abbreviation). Update Ride accordingly so subclasses calling super(name, abbreviation) compile and so students clearly see both attributes must be provided. Ensure the template and solution are consistent with the UML (and task text) so students are not confused about the constructor signature.
